video_title: Jalen Brunson 'separated himself from everybody else on the floor' - Tim Legler | SC with SVP

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's unique ability to control games under pressure
quotes.excerpt: he's one of the rare players that under those circumstances everything narrows for him
quotes.quote: It comes down to a certainty that Jalen Brunson has that most players don't have. He's one of the rare players that under those circumstances everything narrows for him. His focus narrows, his ability—I think because he's more of a grounded player, he's not a player prone to playing vertical or playing supersonic speed downhill. He's going to be under control, on balance, use his strength, his craftiness, his touch to get what he wants, and he controls those possessions, really, I think unlike any other player in the league.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Hart's elite rebounding and energy impact on defense
quotes.excerpt: his rebounding at his size in this league, and this has gone on for a number of years, it's elite
quotes.quote: His rebounding at his size in this league, and this has gone on for a number of years, it's elite. And it gives your defense an element of controlling the end of possessions most teams just don't have from guys that size. He has a nose for the ball, most importantly, he has a lot of want-to. Because that's really what it comes down to: are you willing to go after every one of them? Because you're not going to get most of them.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Karl-Anthony Towns' defensive effectiveness against Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: his size was a factor against Victor Wembanyama and the most important thing, he was able to play without fouling
quotes.quote: His size was a factor against Victor Wembanyama and the most important thing, he was able to play without fouling him. He had one silly foul on a reach when Wembanyama spun near the rim. The rest of it was his close-outs when Wembanyama gets you, and Karl-Anthony Towns is prone to that against any player. He was not picking up those cheap fouls. He was squaring him up under control, and then using his strength against him on those drives because that's where Karl-Anthony Towns has an advantage against him with his size and strength.

quotes.speaker: Jeremy Lin
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs' late-game offensive reliance on Victor Wembanyama isolation
quotes.excerpt: it was too much Victor Wembanyama iso. It just seemed like everything was difficult, everything was hard
quotes.quote: In the fourth quarter, I didn't love the late-game offensive game plan. It was too much Victor Wembanyama iso. It just seemed like everything was difficult, everything was hard, everything was contested. Can we get him in more spontaneous, impulsive actions? Can we get him in some pin-downs? Can he set more screens? Can guards come set screens for him? It felt like every time down the floor they were giving him the ball.

quotes.speaker: Jeremy Lin
quotes.summary_phrase: Keldon Johnson's limited minutes and Spurs' rotation concerns
quotes.excerpt: Keldon Johnson, who played only eight minutes, six man of the year. A lot of minutes went to Harrison Barnes
quotes.quote: Another piece that's really important is Keldon Johnson, who played only eight minutes, six man of the year. A lot of minutes went to Harrison Barnes. I'm not sure what's happening there, but there is going to be a different level of production that needs to be had from other players stepping in. Dylan Harper, obviously an amazing game, but we need the Keldon Johnsons and obviously De'Aaron Fox to be able to step up.
